title: Single page site with anchor navigation
when: The user wants all content on one long page with a nav that jumps to sections.
prompt:
Goal: A long page with a sticky nav, sections that land under the header and a working active state.
Steps:
1. Give every section an id that matches its nav link.
2. Sticky header with nav; add scroll-margin-top on sections equal to the header height.
3. Smooth scroll only inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query.
4. Highlight the current section with IntersectionObserver setting aria-current, not scroll listeners.
5. On phones, collapse the nav into a menu button with aria-expanded.
Quality bar:
- Anchors land with the heading visible.
- Works without JavaScript, only the active state needs it.
- Menu toggle is keyboard friendly.
Pitfalls:
- Headings hidden under the sticky bar.
- Forced smooth scrolling.
- Scroll handlers on every pixel.
Verify:
- [ ] Every nav href matches a section id.
- [ ] scroll-margin-top present.
- [ ] Reduced motion respected.
- [ ] Scripts parse.
Output: index.html, style.css and nav.js.

examples.input: site de uma página com menu fixo
examples.output: sections home, services, prices, contact; sticky nav; active link via observer
